title: The photo corpus has ONE copy: the nightly backup copies the ComfyUI 'output' symlink instead of the images
evidence:
The photo corpus has exactly ONE copy, and the nightly backup does not cover it.

Measured 2026-09-20 from the live mounts and the NAS (read-only):

- Where the bytes are: every photo's `path` resolves into /mnt/nas-ai-models/comfyui-output. The current render mount /mnt/fscache/essdee/ComfyUI/output is a SYMLINK to that NAS tree (same inode verified: 19373054 for gen-1789834527_00001_.png via both paths), so /mnt/fscache holds no image bytes of its own. The NAS tree is the single copy of all 336 photos.

- The nightly backup (/home/tim/backup.sh, 23:30 daily, outside this repo) rsyncs /mnt/fscache/essdee/ to the NAS home backup without --copy-links. rsync therefore copies the `output` entry as a SYMLINK, and on the NAS it is a dangling one: `ls -la ~/backup/essdee/ComfyUI/` -> `output -> /mnt/nas-ai-models/comfyui-output`, `readlink` returns that client-side path, and `ls ~/backup/essdee/ComfyUI/output/` returns 0 entries (no sarah1a3/ either). So the backup covers the ComfyUI app dir and NOT the images -- it looks like it covers essdee while the corpus has no copy in it.

- Even if the symlink were followed, the target (~/backup/essdee) is on the same NAS volume as the mirror, so it would be a same-device copy, not redundancy against volume loss or accidental deletion.

- The dead fallback root that hid this (NAS_OUTPUT_BASE = /mnt/synology-home/backup/essdee/ComfyUI) is a `noauto` CIFS mount of the NAS home: normally NOT mounted (/mnt/synology-home is an empty root-owned dir), and its ComfyUI/output is itself a dangling symlink. That is why the resolver's fallback never resolved -- see the closed entry photo-corpus-bytes-gone, where the same mount was the root cause of 101 photos reading as unrecoverable.

Impact: one NAS volume loss (or one accidental `rm -rf` of comfyui-output, which is a plain directory ComfyUI writes into) destroys every photo the account has ever posted or could post, and nothing in the repo or the backup restores it. 66 photos have ALREADY been lost this way (temp-file renders from /tmp).

This is a backup/infra decision, outside this repo: the fix is either --copy-links plus an off-site target in backup.sh, or an explicit archive step in the harness. Filed, not acted on.
